text: Infinite dragons are dragons who have black scales that echo a blue-white energy and can breathe superheated sand. They are corrupted bronze dragons; who have been led to subvert the timelines by the belief system of a corrupted version of Nozdormu known as Murozond. The titan Aman'Thul blessed the wise Nozdormu and his brood with the ability to time travel and mastery of temporal magic, though the infinites seek to abuse this power to disrupt the timeways to shape a future that is to their ideals. Their nemeses are the Bronze dragonflight, their former kindred, and their ultimate goal is to corrupt the main timeline version of Nozdormu into Murozond to bring about their 'perfected' timeline

Iron Juggernaut is the sixth boss of Siege of Orgrimmar. Created by Siegecrafter Blackfuse, this robotic scorpion guards the gates to the city of Orgrimmar. After it destroys the Darkspear Rebellion's siege weaponry and reserves, the players must destroy the Iron Juggernaut to allow the rebellion into the city.

The Ironforge Airfield, formerly known as the Airstrip or the Dun Morogh airfield, among other (unofficial) things, is an airfield located in a high mountain valley northeast of the dwarven capital city of Ironforge. It has two landing strips, and several gnome pilots are there standing next to their planes or tinkering with them. Around the airfield, there are a series of dwarven buildings and structures. Mountaineers from Ironforge patrol the area, and some members of the Stormpike Guard can be found here too. Isle of Conquest Envoys were orc Isle of Conquest recruiters located at various spots throughout the largest Horde cities - Orgrimmar, Silvermoon City, Thunder Bluff, and Undercity, as well as the neutral cities of Dalaran and Shattrath City. They were only available during the monthly Call to Arms: Isle of Conquest.

The Isle of Thunder is an island found northwest of Kun-Lai Summit and Townlong Steppes. Members of the newly-formed Kirin Tor Offensive and the Sunreaver Onslaught are facing off to lay claim to the isle before the other faction does. Members of the Shado-Pan Assault are united in their singular drive to take down Lei Shen at his seat of power, the Throne of Thunder, once and for all. Thousands of years ago, the Isle of Thunder was known as the Thundering Mountain, home to the mogu's "master". Eventually, Lei Shen defeated his own master and proclaimed himself the ruler of the mogu. He ruled Pandaria from this seat of power until his death. His mogu successors moved the capital to the Mogu'

Jeremy Feasel is a master Pet Tamer located at the Darkmoon Faire on Darkmoon Island, which is only available during the monthly Darkmoon Faire event. He is surrounded by his three level 25 battle pets: Fezwick, Honky-Tonk, and Judgment.

Jintha'Alor (also spelled Jintha'alor) is a forest troll city of the located in the Hinterlands. Jintha'Alor was built by the trolls of the Amani Empire, and named after Jintha, a leader of the Amani in ancient times. It is the second largest city of the forest trolls, second only to Zul'Aman. It was ruled by the Vilebranch tribe for many years and used as a fortress to sacrifice others. The Totem of Akil'darah can be found here. Both the Wildhammer clan and Revantusk tribe laid siege to the city, seeking to end the Vilebranch's incursions upon their land and claim vengeance for their fallen kindred. In the aftermath of this attack, the Revantusk took a step further and claimed the city for

Kargath was at its time the only Horde outpost in Khaz Modan, named after the Shattered Hand clan chieftain Kargath Bladefist. Kargath's flight path was very important because it linked the northern and the southern areas of Horde flight paths on the Eastern Kingdoms. It linked Hammerfall and the Undercity in the north to Grom'Gol, Booty Bay, and Stonard in the south.

Khaz Algar (/ˈkɑz ˈɑlɡɑɹ/ KAHZ AHL-GARR; also known as Sector AR-938) was long-forgotten land mass and is a subterranean continent that is only accessible from an island named Dorn located off the north-western shores of Pandaria. Dornogal, the capital city of the earthen who live on the continent, is the largest settlement.
Kristine Denny represents the Forsaken as a Horde Emissary in Silvermoon City. She can be seen walking with other representatives of the Horde around the streets of Silvermoon City.

Lake Dumont is an extremely large lake with an island in northern Feralas, located just north of Dire Maul near the bordering Desolace and can be reached by foot at north-east of Dreamer's Rest. The island has a ruined mage tower that, judging from the fact it is still burning and the rubble scattered around, some at the bottom of the lake, was probably destroyed not too long ago. There is also a small boat in the lake. The isle also houses several seemingly stranded NPCs. All the NPCs are Alliance, however they're friendly to Horde players. __NOTOC__ Latronicus Moonspear (nicknamed Latro by close friends and family) was a night elf quest giver located in Feathermoon Stronghold in Feralas, specifically in the first building on the right of the path leading away from the flight master. He was one of the community's foremost fighters against the naga. He was killed by naga in an attack on Feathermoon Stronghold shortly after the Cataclysm when he fell behind during the evacuation. Tyrande Whisperwind later found his corpse in one of the buildings.

Keeper Larodar is a keeper located in Lunedane in the Ohn'ahran Plains during Inflammatory Information. Captured by the Druids of the Flame, Enflamed Summoners corrupted him with their fire magic and Fyrakk with shadowflame and appears as Larodar, Keeper of the Flame. This was witnessed by Shandris Feathermoon and an adventurer. She sent her ally to defeat Larodar. During the fight, Larodar summoned Burnt Seed Husks and Rupturing Firevine. After the husks and firewives were destroyed, Larodar heard the call of the Emerald Dream, and he teleported away.

Level has three meanings in World of Warcraft: # Character level: all player characters, mobs and NPCs in World of Warcraft have a level, reflecting their overall effectiveness, power and ability. Player characters can increase their level through gaining experience, granting them access to new abilities, talents and more powerful gear. Higher-level characters have better base stats and generally make more formidable opponents. # Skill level: degrees of advancement in skills (professions) are sometimes called levels. Lexington Mortaim is a Forsaken portal trainer located in the Magic Quarter in the Undercity. Will teach a level 40 Mage the Portal spell to Undercity. He was present during the Battle for Lordaeron and could be evacuated out of the Undercity.

__NOTOC__ Leyline Navigators are nightborne located at the Orgrimmar Embassy in Orgrimmar, and some of them can be seen leaving to Northern Barrens through the Talon Gate. They also appear in Silvermoon City, the Undercity, and the Nighthold in Suramar City following its liberation from the Burning Legion.

Lordaeron City Mutants are mutant creeps found near the ruins of Capital City. In the game, they are creatures similar to the mutants of Dalaran, but being of higher level, heavier, and with magical abilities. They were relatively close to the Garithos base.

The royal palace of Capital City was the seat of power of the kingdom of Lordaeron. Here, King Terenas Menethil II and his ancestors ruled over their country from the imperial chamber. The most significant treaties in all of Lordaeron had been agreed and signed in the imperial hall, which overlooks much of the city. Behind the palace itself are the gardens. The Menethil family resided here, and so did Prince Varian Wrynn during the Second War. Various other guests stayed there over the years such as Muradin Bronzebeard and Thoras Trollbane, king of Stromgarde and friend to Terenas. The Lower City (or Lower Shattrath) is the gathering place for many of the refugees who fled from the war, including arakkoa, sporelings, and almost every other Outland race. It the home to a dozen different faiths and religions and is also described as a coalition. The Lower City of Shattrath is the place where the refugees gather and help out in their own ways. When someone helps any of the mixture of races who fled from war, word gets around quickly. Their quartermaster, Nakodu, is located at the market in the Lower City. The Lunastre Estate is a large residential estate and mansion owned by the aristocratic House Lunastre, and located in the southwest of the nightborne city of Suramar. The estate itself can be found on the city's upper levels, sitting on the very edge of its limits. The compound is quite vast, with extensive gardens, pathways, a mansion, and a panoramic view of the city. The estate is owned by Lady Ly'leth Lunastre, the current head of her family. Owned by one of the more powerful families within nightborne society, the Lunastre Estate is a location of some relative importance and a site of great intrigue for the larger political landscape of the region. Masquerade parties are regularly held

Ly'leth Lunastre is a prominent nightborne noblewoman residing within the nightborne capital city of Suramar. As matron of the aristocratic and powerful House Lunastre, Ly'leth holds great influence among her people. During the Nightfallen insurrection that raged through Suramar, she was a secret member of the rebellion, and used her potent cunning and influence to guide the insurgents' efforts within the city. Ly'leth herself resides in the Lunastre Estate in Suramar City. A socialite, she was well known for throwing lavish masquerade parties and dealing profusely in gossip and rumor-mongering. Magistrates Temple is a beacon of arcane power located somewhere in Dustwallow Marsh that wizards from across Azeroth have traveled to study within. Corrupted by their lust for power, they were hostile to all outsiders that did not share their thirst for magic, and it became overrun with makrura, sea turtles, hydras, spider crabs, Stormreaver and skeletal orcs as well as powerful demons apparently defending the Revenant of Burning Souls. Rexxar and his companions defeated the Temple's denizens and claimed its treasure for the Horde during the events of the Founding of Durotar. There was also a goblin black market.

Magic Mountain is the name of a picture in The Art of World of Warcraft. It is the drawing of a mountain with green sky and magic lightning encircling it. A recolored version of this image can be found as the background image of the warrior's Fury talent tree.

Mana is a magical power resource available to casters which they draw upon when casting spells. It has some parallels with other "bar"-type resources, but unlike the others is consumed relatively slowly. The amount of mana currently available to the caster is denoted with a special blue mana bar below their health bar. By default, casters start with a full bar of mana which is then depleted as they cast spells. Characters have an innate replenishment of both health and mana. Some passive abilities can raise the replenishment rate for these stats independently. During combat mana regeneration is reduced, but some mana can be replenished instantly during combat using mana potions from alchemis

Manaforge Ultris was one of the five facilities that collected the chaotic magic from the Twisting Nether for Kael'thas Sunstrider's blood elves. This manaforge was used beyond its capacity and exploded, creating a tear in the fabric of reality. As a result, it was taken over by creatures from the Void. Before being destroyed, it had Access Shaft Zeon, a mine underneath it that the blood elves used to supply materials for running the manaforges. Ultris is located on a floating island northwest of Tempest Keep.

Mardum, the Shattered Abyss (pronounced mahr-DOOM, colloquially known simply as Mardum and originally called the Plane of Banishment) is a prison world that was created by Sargeras prior to his becoming the Fallen Titan to hold all the demons he killed in the Great Dark Beyond. After his decision to destroy all world-souls in the universe, Sargeras shattered Mardum to free the demons that would become his Burning Legion. Sargeras tasked Brood Queen Tyranna to safeguard the :Sargerite Keystone, a device that can open portals to all Legion worlds, even Argus, on this world. Margoss's Retreat is a floating island just northwest of Dalaran. It contains a large pond and a fishing shack where Conjurer Margoss dwells. Aside from using flying mounts, the retreat can be reached using an Emblem of Margoss or by gliding from the northwestern part of Dalaran (such as with Glide, Emerald Winds or a Goblin Glider Kit). Conjurer Margoss offers teleportation back to the main Dalaran island.

Maxima Blastenheimer is a gnome Darkmoon Faire cannoneer located at the Darkmoon Island, which is only available during the monthly Darkmoon Faire event. She operates the Blastenheimer 5000 Ultra Cannon.
Meditation Manual: Zen Flight teaches the Zen Flight ability, usable by all monks at Level 30 or above and enabling them to fly without a mount.

Mental Quickness is a passive specialization ability for Enhancement Shamans that grants spell power equal to 65% of your attack power, but causes the shaman to no longer benefit from other sources of spell power. It also reduces the mana cost of all instant and totem spells by 75%, reduces mana cost of shocks by 90%, and grants your melee attacks a 40% chance to restore 5% of your mana.

His friend, Steven Thomas, has come to visit him while he is in Silvermoon City with the band and organizing the band's latest tour. He is found at the Walk of Elders with his roadie jungle troll, Roitau. He can also be found near the stage on Darkmoon Island when the isle is opened to the public.

Min'loth the Serpent was a powerful witch doctor in service of Var'gazul. His seat of power was in the city of I'lalai. At one point he was in possession of a bijou. For some reasons, either the plans of conquest, or the water magic used by Min'loth, caused the wrath of Neptulon to come upon an unsuspecting Gurubashi Empire, proving its ultimate downfall. Min'loth was, however, successful in causing pain to the Krakken, a feat not achieved by a mortal in aeons. This only caused the Krakken to become angrier for they are old and they hold many secrets. Mirror Lake is situated in western Elwynn Forest, near an orchard. It is rather small and features a beautiful waterfall. Although Mirror Lake would be an ideal spot for swimming or fishing, the Defias bandits that infest the area make such sports hazardous. After Azeroth had been victim to massive mystic struggles, which tore magic currents from once stable channels, the flow of magic in Stormwind City and Elwynn Forest was somehow altered. Consequently, the mages of the Wizard's Sanctum sent a mage adventurer to Mirror Lake, in order to test its water for magical properties before those who drank from it would be adversely affected. A miracle requests a deity's intercession. One doesn't so much cast a miracle as request one. A person states what he would like to have happen and requests that his Eternal (or the power he prays to for spells) intercede. A miracle can do any of the following things. *Duplicate any healer spell (including spells to which the person has access because of his domains). *Duplicate any other spell, including arcane spells. *Undo the harmful effects of certain spells, such as geas/quest or insanity. Alternatively, a healer can make a very powerful request. Casting such a miracle costs the healer because of the powerful divine energies involved. The Model 4711-FTZ Power Source is a quest item from Apothecary Zinge's field testing quest chain. The power source powers the Field Testing Kit, and in better times it was used by the Gadgetzan Water Company to power water wells in the Tanaris desert. It starts the quest Tanaris Field Sampling.

Moonhunters are a faction within the night elves. They fought alongside the demigod Cenarius with the Shadowleaves, Nightblades, and Starseekers against Grom Hellscream and the Warsong clan. The Nightblades destroyed one of the Warsong bases and the Moonhunters established themselves there, from which they sent periodic attacks against the Warsong clan. However when Grom found the Chaos Well, he and his orcs drank from it and became chaos orcs. With their burst of power they attacked the night elves and killed Cenarius himself.

__NOTOC__ The Moongraze resemble the talbuk of Draenor. Because of this resemblance, some of the refugee draenei who have crashed in the area of these beasts have begun to hunt them as a sort of rite of passage. Acteon, a hunter of Azure Watch, often sends young draenei adventurers to hunt the Moongraze in order to prove themselves ready for future tasks. The Moongraze seem unaffected by the crashed ship and its dangerous power crystals, unlike much of the natural wildlife of Azuremyst.

The monk is a hybrid class, introduced with the Mists of Pandaria expansion. Monks are able to perform each of the three group roles via different specializations: Brewmaster monks tank, Mistweaver monks heal, and Windwalker monks deal damage using melee abilities. Energy is the primary resource of Brewmaster and Windwalker monks (whom also use Chi as a secondary resource), while Mistweavers use mana instead. Monks are available to every race except Dracthyr. Whatever their combat role, monks rely mainly on their hands and feet to do the talking, and on a strong connection with their inner chi to power their abilities. Moon Dance is an ability used by Moon Moon during a Pet Battle.

The Moonlit Landing is a large marina located on the southern edge of the Court of Stars in the nightborne capital of Suramar. As part of the Noble District, the harbor is one of the more affluent areas of the city and services the vast majority of the nightborne nobility, who reside within the nearby districts. After Astravar Harbor, which is found just across the water to the southwest, the Moonlit Landing is the largest series of docks in Suramar, with full access to the surrounding Suramar Bay. Moonrest Gardens are a collection of highborne ruins, including what seems a temple of Elune, located southwest of Stars' Rest in the Dragonblight. Recently, they have been invaded by the blue dragonflight who are attempting to redirect the potent ley lines that lie beneath the surface. Their destructive methods have awoken long-dormant highborne spirits. Surge needles can be found flying over the area.

The Moonwell of Purity is a subzone of Ashenvale near Thunder Peak. It is surrounded by Blink Dragons. This subzone is involved in the quest A Trip to the Moonwell. Shael'dryn was stationed here prior to the Cataclysm. Shaeldryn's Moonwell.jpg|Moonwell of Purity before the Cataclysm.

Mora Woodheart is a Highmountain tauren flying kites with Jaffe Cloudwalker at a cliff southeast of Skyhorn in Highmountain. She also appears at Dazar'alor, flying kites with Jaffe. She is present in Zanchul during Talanji's coronation. By the time of the reawakening of the Dragon Isles, Mora married to Jaffe. She is found at the Wild Coast in the Waking Shores, sitting with Jaffe.
The Moonthorn Bundle would be created by combining Moonthorn Branch. The item would change into a Cleansed Moonthorn Bundle when cleansed in the waters of an ancient moonwell.

Wielding both enchanted warhammers and hand axes, these fierce fighters live to test themselves against worthy opponents. Unconcerned with their race's preoccupation with mechanical devices and mining precious minerals, Mountain Kings live only for battle. Dedicated to safeguarding the Alliance which saved their kingdom during the Second War, the mountain kings can be counted upon to rally behind any banner that stands between freedom and the ever looming shadow of evil.

Mount Farview is a mountain located in the Stonetalon Mountains. The strange configuration of this mountain is such that those standing at or near the peak can see much further, the echoes of the surrounding peaks amplify all sounds, and the winds carry even the slightest scent to every nose. The Awareness Pattern of a ley line is drawn from on top of the mountain.

trailer.]] Mount Kajaro is a still-active volcano on the Isle of Kezan. According to Al'tabim the All-Seeing, Kajaro is an area plagued by volatility - marked by violent and oftentimes magical volcanic eruptions. Kaja'mite was mined underneath it. The Undermine is believed to be situated deep in the bowels of the mountain. __NOTOC__ Mount Mugamba (or Mount Mugambala) is the tallest mountain on Zandalar, located in Zuldazar's western region. The tombs of Atal'Dazar are secluded high atop Mugamba. The Golden Road, beginning at the Temple of the Prophet, is a path up across the mountainside to Atal'Dazar. The Alliance has a camp at Mugamba Overlook at the base of the mountain's northeastern side. The mountain extends north and forms the southern border of Vol'dun, and the southwestern border of Nazmir.

Mountainfoot Strip Mine is a very large mine operation in southwestern Azshara. It is situated in what was formerly the site of the mountain of Forlorn Ridge. It is stated by Horzak Zignibble, and mentioned twice on a Cataclysm preview for Azshara, that the Bilgewater goblins literally moved the mountain to strip mine the minerals below. It is implied that the mountain where Gallywix Pleasure Palace is located is the former Forlorn Ridge. During the Burning Legion's invasion, the mine fell under the Legion's control. Its residents were enslaved by nathrezim and were later killed or rescued by the defenders.

Mount Kra'gor is a mountain located to the east of Gloomshade Grove in . Exile's Rise, Deadwalker Pass and Dol'mak's Hideout are located on the mountain. The Shadowmoon clan's Ancestral Totem is located in a cavern at the mountain's base.

Mount Cortis is a huge mountain in southern Drustvar. Its peak is the highest point in Kul Tiras. Climbing the mountain is possible using several class abilities. Near the summit of the mountain rest the bones of what appears to be a dead demon hunter. At the top, there is a small pile of debris including a sign stating "First".

The green, verdant plains of Mulgore are home to the noble tauren. Mulgore is nestled in the foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains to the north, and protected by a natural wall of mountains on all sides. The only pass through these mountains is currently closed off by the Great Gate, which leads into the Southern Barrens to the east. Mulgore provides bounty for the hunt, as a diversity of wild beasts roam the rolling plains and climb the foothills of the surrounding range. In the northern section of Mulgore, the new Camp Sungraze sits in the shadows of the mesas of Thunder Bluff, a tauren city which towers above the plains. The Mystic Ward is the northwestern district of the dwarven capital of Ironforge and serves as the center for magical activities and study within the kingdom. The Mystic Ward can be accessed via the Commons from the south, the Great Forge from the southeast, and the Forlorn Cavern from the east. Within the district, there are a few shops owned by merchants who cater to mages with their magical goods. In the Hall of Mysteries, which dominates much of the district, are present a number of notable and very powerful magic users, notably class trainers for mages, paladins, and priests. __NOTOC__ Naias is a powerful water elemental summoned by Gift of Naias in Northern Stranglethorn. The human mage Emerine Junis is also trying to get Heart of Naias. Netherwing Ledge is a huge floating island in southeastern Shadowmoon Valley. It is populated by Dragonmaw fel orcs and their nether drake slaves. This land was once held by the Netherwing dragonflight and used it as a breeding area. They kept the Overmine rock flayers, that also inhabitant the area, in check. However, since the nether dragons were run off by the fel orcs, the rock flayers now run rampant. The magic of the Netherwing however is still strong here.
New Moon is a Balance druid ability granted by the Scythe of Elune (artifact). Casting it activates Half Moon (artifact trait), and is activated again after casting Full Moon (artifact trait).

The Nexus is the ancient fortress of the blue dragonflight, found in the center of Coldarra in the Borean Tundra in Northrend. With a network of ice caves underneath, comprising its base, there are rings of floating land stacked upward in a great column over the island, rotating about a massive beam of pure arcane energy. That beam shot into the Twisting Nether and opened rips in reality itself. The Nexus is where Malygos and his dragonflight gathered all that arcane energy during the Nexus War. After Malygos's death, the Nexus stayed standing, though the blue dragonflight was scattered.

No Man's Land is a debuff when the player goes into an area the developers considers "off limits" to characters. Obelisk of the Stars is one of three obelisks in Uldum that were once used to mask the area from the outside world. They also guard an ancient Titan relic. Beneath the obelisk, from four possible entrances, is the Chamber of the Stars. The sand pygmies of the nearby village roam the area with their hyena companions. Oceanmane Village is a small coastal tauren settlement found on the most southwest coast of Kalimdor, near Silithus. It was inhabited by the Oceanmane, but they left long ago. After the Fourth War, Rexxar and Zekhan passed by the village and entered Andrestrasz's lair, and the mok'nathal asked the dragon why he stayed in the village. Andre responded that he couldn't return to his flight until his old Oceanmane friend returned from his hunt, even though it was clear that the tauren brave wouldn't return. Zekhan promised Andre to visit him soon.

Ohn'ahra's Roost is a tall mountain that rises sharply from the north-central Ohn'ahran Plains. As its name suggests, its peak serves as the home of Ohn'ahra herself and a few of her Children. The city of Maruukai rests beside the mountain's southeastern side. Ohn'ahra is initially absent from the roost until the player has completed the Nokhud Offensive dungeon and rescued her from Balakar Khan. A Dragon Glyph required for Ohn'ahran Plains Glyph Hunter is floating above the head of the statue.

Proudmoore Keep is a large castle and palace in the city of Boralus that serves as the seat of power for House Proudmoore, the ruling faction of Kul Tiras. As a result, the keep is also a center of government for Kul Tiras as a whole, and is one of the most fortified locations on the island. Proudmoore Keep can be found in the far west of the city, bordering the areas of Upton Borough, Unity Square, and the Proudmoore Academy to the south and west. The two main entrances, as well as most of the grounds, are protected by the Admiral's Elite Guards.

Qiraji Fortitude is a pet ability available exclusively to the silithid family of hunter pets, increasing player spell power and Stamina by 10%. Due to its tandem benefits, Qiraji Fortitude is functionally superior to the goat family's Sturdiness and the bear family's Invigorating Roar, which only offer Stamina, and to the serpent family's Serpent's Cunning, which only offers spell power. Worthwhile alternatives are the Savage Vigor of the rylak family, which provides a boost to haste instead of spell power, and the Still Water of the water strider family, which provides a boost to critical strike chance instead of Stamina.

Skeletons are undead beings that have been reanimated by magic, often being used as fodder or shock troops by their masters. While gangly and seemingly frail, skeletons can possess superhuman strength and be highly resistant to most physical attacks. Some have retained their consciousness and intellect, and are capable of attacking with weapons and magic. They can be summoned by necromancers, liches, death knights, and dark rangers. Many skeletons are found among the ranks of the Scourge, Forsaken and Knights of the Ebon Blade. In the past skeletons were notably used by the Old Horde and Horde of Draenor.

The Sisterhood of Elune (aka Sisters of Elune or simply the Sisters) could be the oldest night elf religious and magical order, predating the quel'dorei by some 2,000 years. As the name implies, they are an order of priestesses dedicated to the worship and servitude of the moon goddess, Elune. The Sisterhood is led by the High Priestess of Elune, Tyrande Whisperwind, while the priestesses of Elune are the elite of the organization. As followers of the mother moon, they can be found throughout the world, ready to heal the war-weary Azeroth with her holy moonlight. They have existed long before the Great Sundering, and formal worship dates back about 15,000 years.

The Sporemounds were a carnivorous, invasive strain of plant that arose on Draenor during its earliest days. They consumed everything in sight, eventually tapping into the Spirit of Life, allowing all of Draenor's plant life to act as a single organism: the Evergrowth. Zang, Naanu, Botaan, and another unnamed Sporemound were eventually all destroyed by Grond, a mountain given life by the titan Aggramar, and his descendants known as the Breakers. Centuries later, the treant Gnarlgar orchestrated the creation of a new Sporemound called Taala to destroy the Apexis civilization, but it was subsequently destroyed by the Apexis superweapon known as the Breath of Rukhmar.

Stance dancing was the art of changing warrior stances briefly to use abilities from different stances. Talents are special abilities that can be chosen to augment your character. Talents may be passive bonuses or active abilities. Each class has its own selection, with 21 talents split over 7 tiers. Talents are limited by level, with a new tier becoming available each 5-10 levels for all classes. Talents are class-specific, and a majority of choices depend on specialization. Talents offer a further level of customization beyond class and specialization selection, and can be changed very easily and cheaply. In World of Warcraft, a target can mean a few things, primarily the unit that is the current focus of a player's attacks and abilities (or buffs and healing). Other meanings include any unit(s) affected by an ability (even indirectly), a location hit by an area of effect ability, or a strategic objective. Targeting is the act of choosing a target in any of these contexts. Selecting is one form of targeting: choosing one's current target in the user interface, as opposed to the target of an ability or effect. Tatai represents the Darkspear Trolls as a Horde Emissary in Silvermoon City. He can be seen walking with other representatives of the Horde around the streets of Silvermoon City.

Tattered Darkmoon Faire Prize Tickets are the remnants of the original Darkmoon Faire Prize Tickets that were earned during the Darkmoon Faire prior to patch 4.3.0. With the new Darkmoon Prize Ticket currency, these tickets are now obsolete.

The island of Tel'Abim is the home of the popular :Tel'Abim Banana. It could be seen on previous world maps as a large, inaccessible island zone southwest of the Maelstrom and far off the eastern coast of Kalimdor. Not much is known about the island. In Chronicle the island is shown to be southwest of Kezan and east of the Thousand Needles.

Telmor was a hidden draenei-populated city that was once located in Talador on Draenor, now Outland's Terokkar Forest. It was built on a mountainside and was the closest draenei settlement to Auchindoun. The city was located in the middle of ogre country and made invisible by a protective spell using :Leafshadow, a shard of the Ata'mal crystal. The city's leadership resided in the magister's seat, a building that also welcomed Velen whenever he visited.
Teleport: Shattrath is a mage ability that teleports the mage to the Terrace of Light in Shattrath City.
Teleport: Stormwind is an Alliance-only mage teleport that can be learned from any portal trainer. It teleports the caster to the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind City.

The Temple City of En'kilah is a Scourge fortress in the northeastern corner of the Borean Tundra, southeast of the crashed necropolis of Talramas. According to Private Brau, En'kilah is a "plagued Nerubian city". while Muradin Bronzebeard mentioned that the city was built by the Scourge. It is a place of decay and darkness behind stone walls that could have used a steadier hand at the level. Floating above the temple city is another Scourge necropolis, Naxxanar, which served as the command center of the Scourge in the Borean Tundra.

The Teleport to Violet Stand Crystal teleports to the Teleport to Dalaran Crystal at Violet Stand on the western edge of Crystalsong Forest and is used to safely leave Dalaran without having to jump down to the Crystalsong Forest. It is located in the mage portal room just behind on the east side in southeast central Dalaran, to the northwest and across from Krasus' Landing (flight path).

The Teleport to Dalaran Crystal is located in Violet Stand on the western edge of Crystalsong Forest and teleports to the Teleport to Violet Stand Crystal in a portal room in eastern Dalaran just behind , but only if you have used the Dalaran crystal first. Teleport: Dalaran - Northrend is a mage ability that teleports the mage to the Violet Gate in Dalaran above Northrend. This ability can be learned from either a Portal trainer or by completing Attunement to Dalaran.

It was once heavily defended by the Aldor, but now it is defended by the city's newest faction who has taken up residence in the Terrace of Light, the Shattered Sun Offensive. A naaru NPC here will take Heroic Mode instance tokens in exchange for epic items. There is a portal trainer in the middle of the city, affiliated with the Sha'tar faction. Mages are able to learn a teleport spell to Shattrath at level 60 and a portal spell at level 65. The entire promenade hosts a large contingent of Duskwatch security forces, with the attached Sanctum of Order serving as the entity's headquarters. The plateau is connected to the Evermoon Commons district and Shimmershade Garden to the south, as well as the Concourse of Destiny and Terrace of Enlightenment to the east. The terrace is heavily patrolled by Duskwatch forces and, since the arrival of the Burning Legion, even demons. A large tower containing a magical elevator stands on the terrace, and grants instant access to the upper levels of the Sanctum of Enlightenment. The Destruction of Dalaran is the cinematic finale of the Path of the Damned campaign. In this cinematic Archimonde the Defiler disengages from the Twisting Nether and uses a powerful spell to destroy the magic city of Dalaran. (The subtitles of this cinematic are not part of the video; they are displayed through the cinematic subtitles that appear in-game below the video, or in the case of the DVD, as DVD subtitles.).

The Focusing Iris is an orb found in the center of the Eye of Eternity and is used to summon Malygos. An ancient artifact of the blue dragonflight, it is an item of immense arcane power. Keys to the Focusing Iris are held by the most ancient members of the blue dragonflight. At minimal power, they can be used to open the iris a fraction, drawing Malygos's ire. Adventurers of the Alliance and Horde did so during the Nexus War which allowed them to engage and kill the blue Aspect with the help of Alexstrasza.

The Great Akazamzarak is a goblin magician normally found entertaining some Dalaran Citizens at the Eventide in Dalaran. He is an expert with portals and teleportation and is therefore recruited by the Tirisgarde in order to teleport its members inside the Hall of the Guardian, bypassing the security wards. Notably, he was capable of opening and maintaining eight separate portals to various locations scattered across three continents, a feat unprecedented by a single mage in the game.

The Lone Mountain begins the Highmountain storyline. The quest is automatically acquired when players choose Highmountain from their Command Map in their order hall. Like the other three leveling zones, all enemies, quests, treasures, and so forth in Highmountain will scale to the level of the player.

In addition to its inherent strength, Alchemists, Miners and Enchanters can further improve on Thorium (Enchanted Thorium Bar) to allow for the creation of more powerful items. Small Thorium Veins and Ooze Covered Thorium Veins require mining skill 200, Rich Thorium Veins and Rich Ooze Covered Thorium Vein require mining skill 215. The Thorium Brotherhood faction drew its name from the metal, as well. Thor Modan was once the capital of the iron dwarves, though it was destroyed by the stone giants, with much of the main interior of the city in ruins. Thunderstrike Mountain (also called Mount Thunderstrike or simply Thunderstrike) is located in the northeastern part of the Twilight Highlands. The spiritual center of Kirthaven lies within the shadow of the mountain just to the west. The Wildhammers of the Twilight Highlands honor their dead heroes in Kirthaven before burying them with their gryphons atop Thunderstrike, where they are believed to spend eternity at one with the sky. Dwarven cairns and standing stones adorned with gryphon feathers can be found on the summit, while a standard Wildhammer graveyard can be found at the bottom of a passage further down the mountainside. Time-Lost Proto-Drake is an extremely rare monster which occasionally appears among the mountains of the Storm Peaks. It is especially sought after because it has a 100% chance of dropping Reins of the Time-Lost Proto-Drake when killed. Because of its rarity, many players may hunt it for weeks before they even see it at all, much less kill it themselves. The drake is out of reach of ground attacks for most of its flights, and must usually be pulled while on a flying mount or in flight form.

The titans (sometimes capitalized) are a race of colossal, planet-sized cosmic beings, composed of arcane magic and the primordial matter from which the universe was born. They roamed across the cosmos like walking worlds, imbued with the raw power of creation itself. The titans used this incredible force to find and awaken others of their kind. Hailing from the far reaches of the cosmos, they shaped and brought life and order to countless worlds across the Great Dark Beyond. They were described as perfect and majestic beings who are akin to gods.

Zandalari retrieve the spirits within golems through "Soulcatcher Totems". Iridi thought of their appearance not as a shadow, but more akin to the day turning to night, like twilight as experienced on Azeroth. She thus dubbed them twilight dragons.
